Major Developer Documentation Platform GitBook Hit by AI Agent-Driven Attack, Crypto Projects' Docs Affected GitBook reported that attackers used AI agents to gain unauthorized access to some of its infrastructure credentials at 1:00 p.m. EST on November 2. The company detected and blocked the attack, temporarily suspending some services. Potentially exposed data includes integration tokens, Git Sync secrets, API tokens, and visitor questions submitted to GitBook Assistant. No evidence of content modification has been found. GitBook rotated all infrastructure credentials and secrets, revoked all customer API tokens, and advised users to rotate third-party credentials and re-authenticate GitBook MCP connections. By 10:21 a.m. EST on November 3, its app, API, and published docs were accessible again, though some services remained degraded. A full post-incident report is planned. Previously, trade[XYZ] reported unauthorized activity involving its GitBook documentation, which it later restored, and warned users against clicking links during the investigation. PancakeSwap temporarily took its documentation site offline as a precaution following the GitBook security incident and redirected documentation links to its official homepage. — link

Highlight Clip: Bybit CEO: Exchanges Must Prepare for Hacks to Happen(ARCHIVE FOOTAGE) Bybit CEO: Exchanges Must Prepare for Hacks to Happen(ARCHIVE FOOTAGE) On April 21, 2026, Bybit Co-founder and CEO Ben Zhou reflected on the exchange's hack in an interview with The Block. He said one of the biggest shifts in thinking was moving from preventing attacks to assuming an attack will happen, minimizing the damage, and ensuring the company survives. He also discussed Bybit's previous reliance on a third party for its cold wallet. The exchange has since built a banking-grade hardware wallet system requiring staff to be physically present to unlock the HSM. However, such systems are costly and time-consuming to build, so most projects still need to rely on third parties. He said companies should address social engineering alongside technical security and build multiple layers of protection on the assumption that an attack will occur. — link

ZachXBT says $133M theft target is French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa On-chain investigator ZachXBT disclosed on November 4 that the financial institution allegedly affected by a crypto theft exceeding $133 million is Crédit Mutuel Arkéa, a French banking group with approximately $235 billion in assets. ZachXBT previously reported that an EU-based entity was suspected of losing more than $106 million from multiple centralized exchange accounts on November 1. The suspected attacker withdrew funds in USDC and USDT before swapping assets into ETH and privacy coin XMR and transferring funds across multiple blockchains. — link

CoinEx Founder: Binance Incident Exposed Three Entirely Avoidable Security and Operational Flaws Haipo Yang, Founder of CoinEx, stated that the recent Binance security breach exposed at least three critical mistakes that were entirely avoidable, underscoring a failure of operational discipline rather than a lack of sophisticated technology. First, development and operations environments lacked strict isolation; production access should be restricted to dedicated hardware free of third-party software, separating daily communication and browsing onto independent devices. Second, the operations stack lacked meaningful two-factor authentication (2FA), enabling full production compromise via a single leaked credential rather than enforcing hardware-bound MFA through tools like AWS Session Manager. Third, the MPC multi-signature setup existed in name only, as signers failed to conduct substantive independent verifications, causing the entire scheme to collapse upon a single node breach; Yang emphasized that multisig mechanisms are only effective when signers maintain mutual distrust and independently validate each raw transaction rather than blind-signing upstream requests. — link
